title: Vinod Kumar Awasathi v. U.P.P.C.L.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Tarun Agarwala, J.; Vipin Sinha, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; EE to consider objection to provisional theft bill under s.126 and cl. 8.5.
headnote: A provisional bill of Rs. 4,44,025 issued after a checking report found theft of electricity is to be objected to under s.126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and s.8.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A notice already served as objection must be considered by the Executive Engineer, who will pass an assessment order. The writ was disposed without examining the bill on merits.
facts: After a checking report recorded theft of electricity, U.P. Power Corporation Limited raised a provisional bill of Rs. 4,44,025 against Vinod Kumar Awasathi. He invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court. An objection in the form of a notice (annexure 3) had already been served against the provisional bill. Counsel for the petitioner and the licensee were heard by a Division Bench.

holding_units.holding: Where a provisional bill is issued on a checking report finding theft of electricity, objection does not lie in writ. The consumer must file a reply under s.126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and s.8.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; a notice already so filed shall be considered by the concerned Executive Engineer, who will then pass an appropriate assessment order.
holding_units.flag: Court also cites 'Section 8.5' of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; that clause number is not among the catalogued 8.1/8.2 theft-UUE provisions.

not_decided.point: Merits of the theft finding and the quantum of the Rs. 4,44,025 provisional bill
not_decided.note: Left to the Executive Engineer to consider the objection and pass an assessment order.
